note: PASS with caveats. (1) TEXT. Wang (2016) names the instrument ('Dispositional power was assessed via the Sense of Power Scale [1]. This 8-item scale asks respondents to report their beliefs about the power they have. A sample item is ‘I think I have a great deal of power’ (Cronbach's alpha = .71)') and reference [1] is Anderson C, John O, Keltner D (2012) The personal sense of power, J Personality 80:313-344. The study reproduces no items, and its SPSS deposit (PLOS s001, sha256 recorded in .cache) has zero variable and zero value labels, so the words come from the instrument's own English as reproduced verbatim in three independent open-access sources that agree with each other: Ji & Ye (2022) 'Consumers and service robots', J Retailing & Consumer Services (PMC9597570), whose measures appendix prints all eight in canonical order; Li et al. (2023) 'When and why are employees willing to engage in voice behavior' (PMC10111083), whose Appendix A prints them numbered SOP1-SOP8 under the stem 'In my relationships with others'; and Hu et al. (2025) Front. Psychol. (PMC12000008, CC BY 4.0), which states the numbering explicitly -- '4 items (Items 1, 3, 5, 8) were scored in forward ... and 4 items (Items 2, 4, 6, 7) were scored in reverse'. Shipped without terminal periods, matching the PMC10111083 appendix listing; item 5 ships the generalized 'I think I have a great deal of power', which is exactly the sample item Wang quotes, not PMC10111083's negotiation-specific variant. (2) LANGUAGE. Administered in Chinese, no Chinese wording published in the deposit or the paper, so the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: English in the base fields, empty _translated columns, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. (3) ANCHORS. The paper states 'All ratings were made using 5-point Likert scales, ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', which is what option_text carries for the four forward items; for the four reverse-worded items the anchors are FLIPPED to match the stored data, which are already reverse-scored (alpha .713 as stored vs the published .71, and .099 if items 2,4,6,7 are un-reversed) -- same move as burkert_2019_whoqol_bref, disclosed here and in public_note rather than made silently. resp 2-4 are blank because the paper labels only the endpoints. instructions is blank: the paper reproduces no instruction text (only that item order was randomised within each survey), and the 'In my relationships with others' stem seen in PMC10111083 is that study's rendering, not Wang's. (4) MAPPING BASIS = reconstructed. data/wang_2016_authenticity_relationship.py renames S1 columns Power1,P2..P8 -> power1..power8, a number-preserving rename with no positional step, so the code preserves the source's own numbering; but the source carries no text, so WHICH canonical item each number is rests on the standard Sense of Power numbering (corroborated as a convention by PMC12000008 and PMC10111083, not by anything in this dataset). Verification is therefore PARTIAL -- see verify_wang_2016_study1_power.R. (5) STEP 3b. Identity checked, not assumed: 8 items on 1-5 with a per-person sum of 27.71/3.78 and alpha .713 match Table 1's 'Power' row (27.71/3.78) and the Measures alpha of .71 exactly, and the 8 columns are the only power block in the file; the other Study 1 scales (10-item Rosenberg, 12-item authenticity, 7-item Burns relationship satisfaction) are separate IRW tables. (6) RIGHTS: no block. The Sense of Power Scale has no row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be located from the rights holders (Anderson/John/Keltner); they publish no instrument terms page, and the Wiley article carries only the journal's own copyright notice, which is a notice about the article rather than a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). Noted honestly: two later validation papers describe having obtained the authors' permission to reprint the items, which is evidence that someone asked, not a quotable restriction by the holder -- so 'silence is permission' applies. Per the standing rule a round may not write a ship row, so no register row was added. The three sources actually copied from are themselves open (PMC12000008 CC BY 4.0; PMC9597570 and PMC10111083 in the PMC Open Access Subset for unrestricted research re-use).

Two things to read carefully. The four reverse-worded items (power2, power4, power6, power7) are stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED -- Cronbach's alpha of the table as stored is .713 against the paper's published .71, and un-reversing those four collapses it to .099 -- so their option_text is deliberately flipped: resp 1 is 'strongly agree' with the printed statement and resp 5 'strongly disagree', the opposite of the other four items. And which canonical item each code power1..power8 refers to is inferred from the standard Sense of Power numbering: the scale total (27.71, SD 3.78), its correlation with self-esteem (.61) and its alpha all reproduce the paper exactly, but a permutation within the eight items would not be detectable from the data.

note: PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_213). 50 rows = 10 items x resp 1-5; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets exactly. (1) RIGHTS: no block. The RSES register row is a settled verdict=ship on an express public-domain grant from the rights holder ('The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale is now in the public domain, meaning you may use it without charge and without notifying the Sociology Department. This permission extends to making translations or adaptations as you see fit...'), which is applied here, not re-derived; the grant expressly reaches translations, which matters because this is a Chinese administration. (2) STEP 3b: the table is what its name says. 10 items, resp 1-5, n=104, and the live per-person sum reproduces Wang's Table 1 self-esteem M=38.34 SD=5.08 and the alpha of .81 reported in Study 1 Measures; the paper quotes 'On the whole, I am satisfied with myself' as its sample item, which is item 1 of the edition it cites. (3) CODE DERIVATION: data/wang_2016_authenticity_relationship.py melts se1..se10 BY NAME out of s001.sav -- the IRW code IS the source column name, no positional step and no rename (unlike the power/authenticity/relationship blocks in the same script, which are renamed). But the source grants nothing here: s001.sav carries ZERO variable labels and ZERO value labels (checked with pyreadstat: 55 columns, every column_names_to_labels entry None except six Zscore() autolabels; variable_value_labels == {}). So the code is authoritative as an identifier and silent as to content, and mapping_basis is reconstructed, not data_labels. (4) WHICH RSES NUMBERING, and why it matters: the ten RSES sentences circulate in two different orders. The paper's reference [33] is the Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Measures Package edition (1 = 'On the whole, I am satisfied with myself', negatively worded items 2, 5, 6, 8, 9), not the socy.umd.edu order (1 = 'person of worth', negatives 3, 5, 8, 9, 10). The data settle it: see the verification row and verify_wang_2016_study1_se.R -- the cited edition's polarity partition is the top-ranked of all 126 possible 5/5 splits in Study 3 (n=210) and Study 2 (n=191) and rank 2 of 126 here (n=104), while the rival numbering ranks 62nd / 70th / 97th. (5) LANGUAGE, and the mixed fallback -- the main caveat. Study 1's 104 Beijing-area college students answered in Chinese: 'All questionnaires were presented in their Chinese versions. The English scales were translated into Chinese, according to the standard guidelines, by a native Chinese speaker with English as a second language.' The administered Chinese ITEM wording is not recoverable within scope -- the deposit's only files are S1/S2/S3 .sav, none carries a variable label for any se column, there is no questionnaire supplement, and the paper prints one item, in English. So item_text takes the English fallback (text_source=translated_substitute, item_text_translated left empty, language=Chinese as the signal). The administered Chinese ANCHOR wording IS recoverable, and ships: S2 and S3 of the same article attach value labels to the identically named se1..se10 columns -- 1 非常不符合, 2 有些不符合, 3 不能确定, 4 有些符合, 5 完全符合 -- so option_text carries that Chinese verbatim and option_text_translated carries an English rendering written here. Hence translation_source=mixed: the item-level English is the instrument publisher's own (official_instrument_english), the option-level English is machine_translation produced by this project. (6) THE ANCHORS ARE FLIPPED ON FIVE ITEMS, deliberately, against those value labels. The live resp is stored ALREADY REVERSE-CODED: every one of the 45 inter-item correlations in this table is positive (min +0.01), alpha over the stored values is .807 against the published .81, and the raw column sum equals the published total exactly. The same holds in Studies 2 and 3 (alpha .776 vs published .78; .898 vs .90). The S2/S3 value labels were evidently left attached after the recode and are therefore wrong-as-attached for the negatively worded items, the baka2023_bpnsf/burkert_2019_whoqol_bref case: so se2/se5/se6/se8/se9 ship 1=完全符合 .. 5=非常不符合 and the other five ship 1=非常不符合 .. 5=完全符合. This is a deliberate override of a level-1 label, recorded here as required. One consequence: irw-validate may flag resp_ambiguous (two scale directions in one table); that flag is correct about the table and is the whole point of the flip. (7) The paper's own English gloss of the scale, 'ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', is NOT what ships -- the .sav's Chinese is the administered wording and is a better source, and the paper's gloss names only two of the five levels. (8) instructions and section_prompt blank: neither the paper nor any of the three .sav files records an instruction stem, and none was invented. section_id is the trivial wang_2016_study1_se_1; correct_response blank throughout. (9) The alternative reading that was considered and rejected: that no recoding happened and the Chinese version simply reworded all ten items positively. Nothing supports it -- the paper cites Rosenberg (1965) unmodified, quotes a canonical item verbatim, and reports the standard alpha; and the wording method factor is present in all three samples, which is what a half-negative instrument produces and a uniformly positive one does not.

(Front. Psychol., PMC7838489) for items 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11. DEVIATIONS, disclosed: the cic.edu reproduction contains two obvious typos, 'I fell as if I don't know myself very well' (item 7) and 'I am true to myself I most situations' (item 9); both are shipped in the corrected form that the other two sources print ('I feel as if', 'in most situations'). The sources differ on one comma in item 1 -- cic.edu and the Brazilian table print 'to be yourself, than to be popular', PMC7838489 omits the comma; the comma form ships, matching sibling table wang_2016_study1_authliving (batch_212). LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: Study 3's 210 participants were adult Chinese recruited online and answered a Chinese version; the administered Chinese ITEM wording is not recoverable in scope (the only Study 3 deposit file is S3 File, journal.pone.0146050.s003, sha256 07304d590213fe85a43bf61084b0379ba9637efbfa4a0eaf5770d817db0610d7, whose 41 variables carry zero variable labels; there is no questionnaire supplement and the article text prints no Chinese). So item_text takes the fallback -- Wood et al.'s English in the base field, item_text_translated empty, language=Chinese. OPTION TEXT IS DIFFERENT AND IS NOT A FALLBACK: the same .sav DOES carry value labels, identical for all 35 item columns, tying 1.0->'非常不符合', 2.0->'有些不符合', 3.0->'不能确定', 4.0->'有些符合', 5.0->'完全符合', and the processing script's MAP_CN5 maps exactly those five strings onto 1..5. option_text therefore ships the administered Chinese verbatim, with English in option_text_translated. translation_source=mixed accordingly: item_text is the instrument publisher's own English (official_instrument_english), while option_text_translated is IRW's literal English for the five Chinese anchors (machine_translation) -- the paper itself renders only the endpoints, as 'All ratings were made using 5-point Likert scales, ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', which is a gloss rather than a translation of 非常不符合/完全符合, so it was not used. INSTRUCTIONS blank: the paper reproduces no instruction text for Study 3 (only the sentence above, plus 'To control for order effects, we randomized the order of the items within each survey'); nothing literal to transcribe. section_id trivial, section_prompt and correct_response blank. STEP 3b: matches. 12 live items, all 1-5, whose live correlation matrix falls into exactly the three blocks the Authenticity Scale's published key predicts -- {a1,a8,a9,a11}, {a2,a7,a10,a12}, {a3,a4,a5,a6} -- so the table is the 12-item Authenticity Scale and not one of the study's other measures (se1-se10 Rosenberg, p1-p8 power, sd1-sd5 social desirability, all separate tables). VERIFIED PARTIAL (verify_wang_2016_study3_auth.R): routes 5 + 3. All 12 items sit in their canonical block (smallest within-block r = 0.34 vs largest between-block r = 0.47), and the paper's own authenticity total reproduces at M = 38.28 / SD = 6.88 against Table 5's 38.38 / 6.88, with r = .68 to self-esteem and .65 to power against the published .68 and .65 -- which fixes the ascending direction (the reversed coding would read 27.72 and -0.68). Within-block order is NOT pinned; see verification_wang_2016_study3_auth.csv. DATA NOTE, incidental: Wang's stored `authenticity` aggregate is the sum of ELEVEN items -- a1..a12 excluding a11 (recovered by least squares: weights exactly 1 on eleven columns, 0 on a11, max residual 1e-13), and it is that 11-item total, not the 12-item one (M = 42.33, SD = 7.30), that Table 5 publishes. This is a property of the authors' own aggregate column, which IRW does not ship; all 12 items are in the response table. RIGHTS: no block. No row in instrument_rights_register.csv covers the Authenticity Scale. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be located or quoted for it: the cic.edu PDF distributes the full scale with its scoring key and states no terms, the Brazilian validation and PMC7838489 reproduce all 12 items with no use restriction, and the 2008 APA article carries only its own copyright notice, which is a notice about the article rather than a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). Shipped under 'silence is permission'; per the rule that a round may write only block rows, no ship/ship_with_note register row was written. Same finding as sibling wang_2016_study1_authliving (batch_212), reached independently.
